page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The instance profile includes no local storage volumes and no discrete GPU acceleration, while provisioning a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a pronounced contrast between single-thread and multi-thread execution. Single-core performance sits in the lower tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0 and single-threaded gzip compression measured at 18.89 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics match mid-range expectations, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 5755.0, clang software compilation scoring 10657.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 57.1 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects solid operational capacity, highlighted by 11.3 million Redis SET operations per second and an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 76.43 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides qualitative resource efficiency when memory capacity is the principal constraint rather than per-thread processing speed. Because no bundled local storage is included, root and data persistence rely entirely on remote network storage. Workload profiles that align with this hardware balance include distributed in-memory data stores like Redis, relational database nodes, and intermediate data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory residency.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense deployments. The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes and providing a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate modest single-thread CPU performance paired with standard multi-threaded throughput, reaching 5755.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 11.3 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. With solid memory bandwidth and significant RAM capacity, this server is appropriate for in-memory database caching, relational database services, and ETL staging tasks where memory footprint outweighs single-core compute performance requirements.
